talk_track: I spend my time on one narrow problem: a data platform assembled out of acquisitions, where the reporting carries a statutory deadline and two or three people hold the whole thing in their heads. Your open Data Transformation Manager role is responsible for "ensuring accurate, efficient, and seamless data conversions while maintaining enterprise-wide data quality, hygiene, and coverage." Those are opposite jobs sharing one calendar - a conversion is a project with an end date, while hygiene across the partner firms that same posting names is a permanent operation that grows the day you sign the next one. When one hire owns both, conversions always win, because conversions have the visible deadline, and the quality tooling stays a backlog item until a filing season exposes it. The cheap move is separating the two on paper before the offer goes out - name who owns conversion throughput and who owns standing data quality, even if it is the same person this year. Is that role expected to carry the ACT book conversions as well?
